new_scholarship.name: Annual scholarship programme for foreign citizens offered by Romania through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Government Decision no. 288/1993)
new_scholarship.official_source: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Romania (Ministerul Afacerilor Externe, MAE)
new_scholarship.duration: 3-6 years for the bachelor's cycle depending on the specialization, plus a financed Romanian-language preparatory year where applicable
new_scholarship.deadline: Official wording: 'The enrolment period begins on 16 February 2026. The deadline for submitting applications is 31 March 2026.' Applications are submitted exclusively online, via the dedicated platform.
new_scholarship.application_period: 16 February 2026 to 31 March 2026 for the 2026-2027 cycle; the selection results were announced by e-mail around 15 July 2026. The programme is annual, so a 2027-2028 cycle is expected, but no official opening date or deadline for that cycle had been published as at the verification date.
new_scholarship.application_method: Separate application submitted by the candidate directly and exclusively online on the MFA-run Study in Romania scholarship platform at https://scholarships.studyinromania.gov.ro/ (reachable from studyinromania.gov.ro via the 'Apply for MFA scholarships' button; the platform is in English and French). It is not automatic on admission. The official programme information states that applications submitted directly to the registry offices of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs or the Ministry of Education and Research, or to the e-mail addresses of MFA employees or departments, or to the Romanian diplomatic missions or the foreign diplomatic missions accredited in Bucharest, 'will not be taken into consideration'.
new_scholarship.description: Romania's Ministry of Foreign Affairs provides an annual scholarship programme for foreign citizens from all non-EU countries to study at accredited Romanian higher education institutions, based on Government Decision no. 288/1993. For the bachelor's and master's cycles only Romanian-language study programmes are available, and candidates who do not speak Romanian are granted a financed Romanian-language preparatory year before the degree programme. Scholarships are awarded through a competition of files conducted jointly by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Ministry of Education and Research, and cover tuition, dormitory accommodation within an allocated subsidy, and a monthly scholarship paid in Romanian lei.
new_scholarship.best_fit: Non-EU citizens who hold a baccalaureate degree or equivalent with an average of at least 7 on the Romanian scoring system (or the 'Good' grade), are willing to study in Romanian or to complete a financed Romanian-language preparatory year, and can obtain apostilled or authenticated study documents, a valid passport and authorized translations before the deadline.
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: Foreign citizens from all non-EU countries, with statutory exceptions: citizens of Romanian origin or of the Romanian historical communities near Romania, persons who have requested or acquired a form of protection in Romania, recognized stateless persons resident in Romania, members of the diplomatic and consular corps and their families accredited to Romania, members of the administrative and technical staff of diplomatic missions, staff of international organizations based in Romania and their families, and existing beneficiaries of a Romanian state scholarship for the same cycle of study. For the bachelor's track the applicant must be a graduate of high-school or pre-university studies holding a baccalaureate degree or equivalent, or a candidate applying for further university studies in Romania, with an average of the study years for the last graduated school of at least 7 (seven) corresponding to the Romanian scoring system or the 'Good' score. There is no age limit. Scholarships are not awarded in Medicine, Dental Medicine or Pharmacy, and bachelor's programmes are taught only in Romanian. A complete file, a valid passport, and apostille or authentication of all study documents are mandatory.

new_scholarship.selection_notes: Scholarships 'are awarded through a competition of files based on the regulations in force, by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) and the Ministry of Education and Research'. Selection is therefore a central, file-based competition with no published weighting, interview or portfolio component for the bachelor's track. The published academic threshold is an average of at least 7 (seven) on the Romanian scoring system, or the 'Good' score, for the last graduated school, and the file must be complete, with study documents from accredited institutions, apostilled or authenticated, and a valid passport. Results are announced by e-mail to every candidate; for the 2026-2027 cycle this was around 15 July 2026. An admission interview forms part of the selection only for doctoral studies. Applicants who applied in previous years are not disadvantaged, as results from previous years are not taken into account.
new_scholarship.image_alt_text: Ministry of Foreign Affairs Scholarships - Study in Romania
new_scholarship.notes: The programme also funds the master's cycle (1, 1.5 or 2 years) and the doctoral cycle (4 years); this record documents the bachelor's track, with degree_levels set to "Bachelor's" and the wider cycle coverage noted here and in funding_duration. No monetary amount is published on any reachable official page: the FAQ grants only 'a monthly financial aid, in accordance with the legislation in force', and the official scholarships overview states that the amount and number of state scholarships are set by Government decision and that they are awarded in Romanian lei, so funding_amount, funding_currency and funding_period are null rather than estimated. International transport, personal expenses and visa costs are not covered, and dormitory accommodation is provided only within the allocated subsidy and to the extent of available places, so the award is recorded as Partially Funded with fully_funded false. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs own site www.mae.ro and its embassy subdomains returned HTTP 503 on every fetch attempt, so the ministry summary page and the embassy-hosted 'Annex no. 1 / Information on the Scholarship Programme' PDF could not be read; the identical programme information was read on the MFA-run official scholarship platform. Two official sources conflict on the preparatory-year exemption: the scholarship platform requires study documents or school records attesting at least three consecutive years of study in Romanian, while the Study in Romania scholarships overview says at least four consecutive years; the programme-specific platform text was used. verification_confidence is capped at 0.7 because an official page was unreachable. The 2026-2027 cycle closed on 31 March 2026, so the record is marked closed and carries the next-cycle expectation; the expected 2027-2028 timing is an inference from the two most recent cycles (2025-2026 closed 12 March 2025; 2026-2027 closed 31 March 2026) and is not an official announcement. SCHEMA_CONTRACT.md v2 refers to 'today' as 2026-10-03; the actual verification date of 2026-10-10 is used throughout this record.

programme_detail_official.application_cycle: 2026-2027 cycle (applications open 16 February 2026, deadline 31 March 2026, results by e-mail around 15 July 2026); the programme is annual under Government Decision no. 288/1993 and a 2027-2028 cycle is expected, with no dates yet published
programme_detail_official.deadline_central_display: 31 March 2026. Official wording: 'The enrolment period begins on 16 February 2026. The deadline for submitting applications is 31 March 2026.'
programme_detail_official.deadline_note: A single central deadline of 31 March 2026 applied to the 2026-2027 cycle and applications were submitted only through the online platform, so no separate institutional or national deadline exists. No deadline time or timezone is published; the official wording gives a calendar date only. The host university's own enrolment conditions (additional documents, aptitude tests, registration deadline) apply only after selection and are later formalities, not earlier deadlines. This deadline has passed, so the cycle is closed; the next cycle's dates are not yet published, and the expected timing around February-March 2027 is an inference from the two most recent cycles rather than an official announcement.
programme_detail_official.status_note: The 2026-2027 cycle opened on 16 February 2026 and closed on 31 March 2026. The official results page confirms that applications are closed and that selection results were e-mailed to candidates around 15 July 2026, with 88,798 applicants from 152 countries competing in that cycle. The programme is annual, so a 2027-2028 cycle is expected; based on the two most recent cycles (2025-2026 closed 12 March 2025; 2026-2027 closed 31 March 2026) the next application window is expected around February to March 2027, but no official date had been published at the verification date.
programme_detail_official.funding_duration: A monthly scholarship is granted for students enrolled in the Romanian-language preparatory year and for students enrolled in bachelor's, master's or doctoral studies, but 'not more than the duration of a university cycle'; tuition is financed for the preparatory year and the degree programme on the same limit. The bachelor's cycle runs 3-6 years depending on the specialization, so total support can span the preparatory year plus up to six study years for the longest programmes.
programme_detail_official.tuition_coverage_note: Tuition is financed for the Romanian-language preparatory year and for the actual studies, 'but not more than the duration of a university cycle, corresponding to the study programme followed'. It is not recorded as unconditionally fully funded: the official scholarships overview states that state scholarships 'do not cover personal expenses and international transport'; the student must carry out all steps for lodging a visa application and bear all costs inherent to it; dormitory accommodation is financed only within the allocated subsidy from the Ministry of Education and Research budget and is provided to the extent of available places; and no monetary amount is published anywhere on the reachable official pages, so the real value of the stipend cannot be confirmed from the official source.
programme_detail_official.funding_label: Tuition (Romanian-language preparatory year and degree programme) plus dormitory accommodation within the allocated Ministry of Education and Research subsidy, and a monthly scholarship paid in Romanian lei with the amount set by Government decision and not published; international transport, personal expenses and visa costs are not covered.

eligibility: Foreign citizens from all non-EU countries, with the statutory exceptions listed under ineligibility_conditions.

programme_detail_official.citizenship_residency: Restricted by nationality: foreign citizens from all non-EU countries are eligible, and citizens of EU member states cannot use this programme. No residence requirement is published; residence outside Romania is neither required nor considered. Certain categories of persons present in or accredited to Romania are excluded by statute rather than by residence.
programme_detail_official.international_eligibility: Open to applicants from all non-EU countries worldwide. Candidates of any nationality outside the EU may apply from anywhere, and 152 countries were represented among the 88,798 applicants in the 2026-2027 cycle.
programme_detail_official.study_mode: Full-time on-campus study at an accredited higher education institution in Romania; the Romanian academic year usually begins on 1 October and each university sets its own calendar. Bachelor's and master's programmes are available only in Romanian, so non-Romanian speakers complete a financed Romanian-language preparatory year before the degree programme.
programme_detail_official.research_requirement: None for the bachelor's track. A research requirement applies only to the doctoral cycle, which additionally requires the written agreement of a Doctoral Tutor who is a member of the doctoral school and the passing of an admission interview.
programme_detail_official.subject_or_agency_requirement: No nominating agency or university nomination is required; candidates apply directly to the central platform. Field restriction: applicants may select their programme of interest in all fields, 'with the exception of Medicine, Dental Medicine and Pharmacy', for which scholarships are not awarded.
programme_detail_official.application_method: A separate application, submitted by the candidate directly and exclusively online on the MFA-run Study in Romania scholarship platform; it is not automatic on admission and no university application substitutes for it. Applications submitted directly by the applicants to the registry offices of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs or the Ministry of Education and Research, or to the e-mail addresses of MFA employees or departments, or to the Romanian diplomatic missions or the foreign diplomatic missions accredited in Bucharest, are explicitly rejected. Only one application may be submitted during each programme and the profile cannot be edited after submission.
programme_detail_official.application_route: Create an account at https://scholarships.studyinromania.gov.ro/ (reachable from studyinromania.gov.ro via the 'Apply for MFA scholarships' button), complete the online form, upload each document as an individual .pdf scan made after the original, sign the GDPR declaration, and submit before the deadline.

programme_detail_official.english_requirement_note: No English-language test or score is required for the bachelor's track and none is published. The language requirement is Romanian, because bachelor's and master's programmes are taught only in Romanian; it is satisfied by the financed Romanian-language preparatory year, or by exemption through Romanian study documents or school records attesting at least three consecutive years of studies in Romanian in the Romanian national system, passing the Romanian language test, or presenting a certificate of linguistic competence in Romanian at minimum level B1. English, French and Spanish function only as permitted languages for authorized translations of documents, and the Curriculum Vitae must be written in English, French or Romanian.
selection_criteria: Awarded through a competition of files based on the regulations in force, by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Ministry of Education and Research.

programme_detail_official.duration: 3-6 years for the bachelor's cycle depending on the specialization followed, ending with a bachelor's exam; a Romanian-language preparatory year is additionally granted for candidates who do not speak Romanian. The master's cycle runs 1, 1.5 or 2 years and the doctoral cycle 4 years.
award_holder_conditions: Respect the Romanian Constitution and the laws of the Romanian state.
Comply with the internal regulations of the educational institution in which they study.
Comply with the provisions of the programme methodology.
Present, at enrolment, a medical certificate stating that they are fit for studies and free of contagious diseases, with authorized translation.
Carry out the necessary steps for lodging a visa application for Romania and bear all costs inherent to it.
The granting of the scholarship automatically ceases if the student loses student status.
Facilities are lost if the student does not attend classes at the minimum percentage stipulated by the institution's regulations.

Facilities are lost if the student does not meet the minimum number of transferable ECTS credits applicable to Romanian citizens, required for passing the Romanian language preparatory year and for advancing to the next academic year.
Facilities are lost if the student is expelled in accordance with the institution's own regulations.
Facilities are lost if the student changes their field of study at the bachelor's, master's or doctoral level.
Facilities are lost if the student breaches the obligations set out in the university study contract or the internal regulations of the institution.
Facilities are lost if the student requests this in writing.

The scholarship cannot be suspended or transferred to the next academic year, and cannot be reinstated after loss through expulsion, a change of field of study, breach of contract, or a written request.

The scholarship may be reinstated after loss through insufficient attendance or credits only if the student meets the minimum attendance and ECTS requirements in the following academic year, and provided the total scholarship years do not exceed the duration of the study cycle.

The candidate's university option cannot be guaranteed: the Ministry of Education and Research may propose an alternative in the same field of study subject to availability, and subsequent requests to change the field of study or the university will not be taken into consideration.
supplements_or_initiatives: Romanian bilateral or multilateral inter-governmental and intercultural agreement scholarships (a separate category of state scholarship for non-EU students).

programme_detail_official.description: The annual scholarship programme for foreign citizens offered by Romania, through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, based on Government Decision no. 288/1993. Scholarships for studies in accredited higher education institutions in Romania are awarded through a competition of files based on the regulations in force, by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Ministry of Education and Research. The programme covers the bachelor's, master's and doctoral cycles and finances tuition, dormitory accommodation within an allocated subsidy, and a monthly scholarship paid in Romanian lei.
programme_detail_official.coverage: Tuition for the Romanian-language preparatory year and for the degree programme up to the duration of the university cycle; a monthly scholarship paid in Romanian lei for both the preparatory year and the degree programme; dormitory accommodation within the allocated Ministry of Education and Research subsidy; and exemption from registration and application-processing fees. International transport, personal expenses and visa costs are not covered.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your non-EU citizenship and work through each of the seven statutory exclusion categories before you invest time in the file.
Confirm you hold a baccalaureate degree or equivalent, or a certificate proving you passed the baccalaureate exam, since the diploma must be held at the time of submission.
Calculate the average of your study years for the last graduated school and check it against the 7/10 threshold or the equivalent 'Good' grade.
Start apostille or authentication of every study document immediately when the call opens, and confirm your country's status under the Apostille Convention.
Arrange authorized translations into English, French, Spanish or Romanian for every document that is not already in one of those languages.
Obtain or renew your passport before the call so the first three pages can be uploaded on time.
Write your CV in English, French or Romanian and align it with the field of study you will select.
Decide your Romanian-language route: the financed preparatory year, the Romanian language test, or a B1 competence certificate.
Register on the platform early, because you can submit only one application and cannot edit it afterwards.
Exclude Medicine, Dental Medicine and Pharmacy from your shortlist before you build the application.
Budget in advance for flights, visa fees and personal living costs, which the scholarship does not cover.
Plan for a one-year language year if you do not speak Romanian, so your degree start date is realistic.
common_rejection_risks: Study documents that are not apostilled under the Hague Convention or authenticated by the home-country authorities - the official announcement warns that non-compliant applications may be deemed ineligible.
Applying without a valid passport, or with a passport whose first three pages are not uploaded.

Submitting the application by e-mail or post, or through the MFA or Ministry of Education registry offices, MFA staff e-mail addresses or a diplomatic mission - such applications are rejected outright.
An average below 7 on the Romanian scoring system, or below the equivalent 'Good' grade, for the last graduated school.
Study documents from institutions that are not accredited or recognized in the country where they were issued.
An incomplete file: any missing diploma, transcript, birth certificate, passport page or CV makes the application invalid.
Documents not scanned individually after the original in .pdf format, or missing authorized translations.
Failing to sign the GDPR declaration, which is required for the registration to be valid.
Selecting Medicine, Dental Medicine or Pharmacy, which are excluded from the scheme entirely.
Submitting more than one application during the programme, or assuming the file can be edited after submission.
Missing the central deadline; there is no late window and no institutional fallback deadline.
estimated_uncovered_costs: International transport to and from Romania: the official scholarships overview states that state scholarships do not cover international transport.
Visa application costs: recipients must carry out all steps for lodging a Romanian visa application and bear all costs inherent to it.
Personal expenses generally, which are explicitly not covered.
Food: the official cost-of-living guidance estimates EUR 150-400 per month for canteen, groceries and eating out.

Accommodation if no subsidized dormitory place is available: dormitory places generally start from about EUR 80 per month, a room in a shared apartment under EUR 250 per month, and a full apartment EUR 400-650 per month in Bucharest, Cluj-Napoca, Iasi or Timisoara.
Medical insurance: from about EUR 40 per month, private or through the state insurer.
Phone and internet: EUR 20-60 per month; gas and electricity: EUR 80-150 per month.
Public transport: EUR 20-60 per month, before the student transport discounts.
Any tuition, fee or accommodation cost falling beyond the financed duration of the university cycle.
document_audit: Every document must be scanned individually, after the original, in .pdf format - not as one merged PDF and not as photographs.
The passport requirement is specific: the first three pages of a valid passport, and the passport must still be valid.
The birth certificate is required even though it is rarely requested by other scholarship schemes, so request a certified copy early.
The CV must be in English, French or Romanian; the diploma and transcript translations may be into English, French, Spanish or Romanian.
All study documents need an apostille or authentication before translation is useful, so sequence notarization, apostille and translation deliberately.
If you have not yet received your diploma, the certificate proving you passed the baccalaureate exam is the substitute document, with an authorized translation.
The parental consent declaration is only relevant if you will be under 18 when courses start; it must be notarized and translated.
If you have already completed the preparatory year or hold a Romanian competence certificate, include that certificate - it is what earns you the exemption.
The GDPR declaration is a signature on the platform, not an uploaded document, but the registration is invalid without it.
The medical certificate is not part of the scholarship application; it is requested later, at enrolment, by the host university.

alerts.trigger: You are relying on the 2026-2027 cycle
alerts.message: The 31 March 2026 deadline has passed and applications are closed; results for that cycle were e-mailed around 15 July 2026. Wait for the next annual call, expected in the first quarter of 2027, and re-check the official announcement page before preparing documents.

Bachelor's programmes are taught only in Romanian, so plan on a financed preparatory year before your degree starts. If you have Romanian study documents or school records covering at least three consecutive years of study in Romanian, you can claim an exemption, as you can by passing the Romanian language test or presenting a B1 competence certificate.

alerts.trigger: Your study documents are not yet apostilled or authenticated
alerts.message: This is the most common cause of ineligibility under the updated rules. Start authentication as soon as the call opens and confirm whether your country is party to the Apostille Convention; non-compliant applications may be deemed ineligible.

alerts.trigger: You do not yet hold a valid passport
alerts.message: A valid passport is mandatory and you cannot apply without one. Obtain or renew it before the application window opens, because you cannot edit your file after submitting.

alerts.trigger: You were counting on an English-taught bachelor's programme
alerts.message: At bachelor's and master's level only Romanian-language programmes are available. Only doctoral scholarship holders may opt for a foreign language set by the doctoral school, so choose a Romanian-taught programme or a different scheme.

alerts.trigger: You want to keep the option of changing university or field after selection
alerts.message: Changing your field of study is a ground for losing the scholarship, and if your first-choice university cannot be honoured the Ministry of Education and Research may place you at another institution in the same field, with later change requests not considered.

alerts.trigger: You want to defer your start by a year
alerts.message: The scholarship cannot be suspended or transferred to the next academic year. Only accept if you can enrol in the year for which the award was made.

alerts.trigger: Your country is not party to the Apostille Convention
alerts.message: Authentication by the relevant authorities in your home country, such as the ministry of education, is the alternative route. Check processing times early, because these chains often take longer than the application window.

alerts.trigger: You are treating this as your only application
alerts.message: 88,798 applicants from 152 countries competed for the 2026-2027 cycle. Apply in parallel to other European bachelor's funding routes so a single competitive outcome does not decide your plans.

submission_workflow: Read the official programme information and FAQ in full on the scholarship platform, and confirm you meet every eligibility condition.
Create an account on https://scholarships.studyinromania.gov.ro/ as soon as the call opens.
Prepare and upload each required document as an individual .pdf scan made after the original, with authorized translations where applicable.
Complete the online application form: personal data, contact details, academic background and preferred study domains.
Sign the GDPR declaration of consent so the registration is valid.
Submit the application before the deadline and keep the on-platform confirmation plus the e-mail notification of successful submission.
Wait for the e-mail announcing the evaluation results, sent to every candidate around 15 July 2026 in the 2026-2027 cycle.
Reply by e-mail to accept or refuse the offer; if you refuse, do so quickly so another candidate can be selected.
On acceptance, download the scanned Letter of Acceptance for Studies in Romania and apply for the long-stay study visa, bearing all visa costs yourself.
Contact the host university to learn its enrolment conditions and prepare the enrolment file, including the medical certificate.

Present yourself at the Office of International Relations or Rector's Office within the period indicated, with the original documents, the letter of acceptance, your passport with a valid visa and the medical certificate.
Keep your attendance and ECTS credits at or above the minimum applicable to Romanian students for the whole cycle, because falling short ends the scholarship.

research_notes.logo: The logo is served from the awarding programme's own domain: https://scholarships.studyinromania.gov.ro/src/org/mae/template/images/mae-scholarships.svg (58479 bytes, probed live, HTTP 200, Content-Type image/svg+xml). It is the brand mark used in the header of every page of the official MFA scholarship platform, so it belongs to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs scholarship programme rather than to any host university or third party. It was read in full: the wordmark uses dark fills (#0071BC blue and #575756 grey) rather than a white-on-transparent treatment, so it is visible on a light card and is not excluded by the white-wordmark rule. Two further marks on the same domain were probed as alternatives (study-in-romania-logo.svg, 4061 bytes; logoro.svg, 23791 bytes) and also returned image bytes, but the header brand was chosen as the programme-specific mark. The host scholarships.studyinromania.gov.ro was not already present in backend/config/official_logo_overrides.json, so no deduplication is expected.

research_notes.degree_level_confirmed: The official programme information on the MFA scholarship platform states that 'bachelor's degree: bachelor's degree programmes are addressed to graduates of high school studies or pre-university studies at the end of which they obtained a baccalaureate degree or equivalent, as well as candidates applying for further university studies in Romania. The complete programme runs for a period of 3-6 years, depending on the specialization followed and ends with a bachelor's exam'. The official cycle announcement repeats the same three study cycles, and the FAQ lists Bachelor, Master and PhD. The programme also funds the master's and doctoral cycles, so degree_levels is set to "Bachelor's" for this record and the wider coverage is recorded in funding_duration, programme_structure notes and the record notes, as required by the degree-level rule.
